newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran facts at a glance.
newsitem.headline: Iran facts at a glance.

text.p: Here are key facts about Iran:
POPULATION: About 60 million according to 1996 census, comprising many ethnic groups of Aryan or Turkic descent, with some Arabs in the south. Growth rate 2.5 percent a year.
RELIGION: Mostly Shi'ite Moslem, with some Sunni Moslems, Baha'is, Orthodox Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians.

AREA: 1,648,184 sq km (650,095 sq miles), bordered by Armenia, Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan to the north, Turkey and Iraq to the west, Afghanistan and Pakistan to the east. Southern coast extends from the head of the Gulf to the Indian Ocean.
CAPITAL: Tehran. Population 6.6 million according to the census but 10 million by unofficial estimates.

ECONOMY: Gross domestic product 186.125 trillion rials in 1995-96. Annual inflation 23.2 percent in the Iranian year ended March 1997. Iran is heavily dependent on revenue from oil exports. It is the world's third largest exporter after Saudi Arabia and Norway. It has 90 billion barrels of proven oil reserves, about 10 percent of the world total. Daily output around 3.6 million barrels. It has the world's second largest proven natural gas reserves after Russia. It shares with Qatar the world's largest gas field, North Dome.
EXCHANGE RATE: The official rate for calculating state budget accounts is $1=1,750 rials. Rate for exports is $1=3,000.
ARMED FORCES: 513,000, about half of whom are conscripts. Equipment includes 1,440 tanks, 295 combat aircraft including 30 MiG-29s, and three Russian Kilo-class submarines.
